The University of Heidelberg offers an exceptional research environment, and the expectation is that post-doctoral researchers pursue independent high-quality academic research. Research activities (such as presenting at international conferences) will be actively supported by the chair and generous funding is available. Other tasks include contributions to external grant applications, as well as contributions to the chair’s teaching portfolio and supervision of degree theses. The formal teaching requirement for the position is two weekly contact hours per semester (SWS).

Application Process

As an equal opportunity employer, Heidelberg University actively encourages applications by women. Preference will be given to disabled applicants with equal qualifications. For full consideration, please submit your application (cover letter explaining your interest in the position, CV including hyperlinks to research papers, a job market paper, and two or more reference letters) via econjobmarket.org by 15 November 2026 (12:00 a.m. UTC).

Virtual interviews will be held in December 2025, primarily as part of the European Job Market.

For further information about the position, contact Prof. Simon Görlach PhD (simon.goerlach@awi.uni-heidelberg.de).
name: Heidelberg University

adtitle: Senior Research Fellows/Postdocs (m/f/d) in Management / Economics of Innovation
adtext:
The department of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Research at the Max Planck Institute for Innovation and Competition conducts research on the incentives, determinants and implications of innovation and entrepreneurship processes, as well as their behavioral foundations. It is headed by Prof Dietmar Harhoff, PhD.

We are seeking a Senior Research Fellows/Postdocs (m/f/d) in Management / Economics of Innovation effective immediately.

  • The term is up to 2 years.
  • The expected start date is February 2027, deviations are possible.
  • There are no teaching obligations.
  • There is no tenure-track.
  • The gross salary is based on the German Labor Agreement for Public Service (TVöD), level E13.
  • Candidates must hold a doctoral degree in management, business administration, economics or a related field by the end of the year they start their employment.

Researchers at the Institute are expected to independently carry out basic research in the fields of

  • Innovation (with a possible focus on intellectual property rights, digitalization and innovation, origins and impact of AI, science of science, organization of innovation processes, innovation policy, innovation addressing grand challenges)
  • Entrepreneurship (e.g., entrepreneurial finance, start-up acceleration, entrepreneurship education, social and inclusive entrepreneurship)
  • Behavioral Foundations (e.g., incentives for creativity, innovation motives and behavior, inventor characteristics)

The Max Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of women in areas where they are underrepresented and therefore strongly encourages women to apply. The Max Planck Society is committed to employing more people with disabilities and expressly encourages them to apply.
name: Max Planck Institute for Innovation and Competition

adtitle: Postdoc in AI agents and human-AI interactions in financial systems
adtext:
Institut Louis Bachelier (Paris) and Toulouse School of Economics are offering a postdoctoral position funded by INESIA (National Institute for Artificial Intelligence Assessment and Safety) for a research project on "AI Agents and Human-AI Interactions in Financial Systems: Alignment, Behaviors, and Systemic Risks" led by Marie Briere (ILB) and Milo Bianchi (TSE). The project aims at understanding how AI agents and human-AI interactions may create new systemic vulnerabilities in financial markets.

The position starts as soon as possible (flexible start date) and is available for 2 years. The main location is either ILB (Paris) or TSE (Toulouse), upon mutual agreement.

The candidate should have strong interest in the modeling of AI agents and ideally expertise in the design of hybrid experimental markets with AI agents and human subjects and in the implementation of AI agent simulations in fictitious financial markets.

The fellow is expected to contribute as a co-author on a project paper and/or provide support to other members of the research team. Active participation in TSE's and ILB's academic life is also expected. Knowledge of French is not required.

Application deadline: November 10th, 2026

Applications should include:

  • a CV
  • a cover letter with a short research statement (1 page max)
  • at least one academic paper
  • at least two recommendation letters

Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an online interview in November 2026.

Contacts:

Marie Briere - marie.briere@institutlouisbachelier.org

Milo Bianchi - milo.bianchi@tse-fr.eu

adtext:
CALL FOR APPLICANTS: Junior Economist
ASBL/2026-02

STATEC Research is looking for a junior researcher to join the research department of the Statistical Office of Luxembourg (STATEC). This is a full-time position based in Luxembourg. The initial appointment is for two years, with the possibility of extension. We offer an attractive salary and research allowance. Social insurance, including a pension scheme and health insurance, is included in the salary.

STATEC Research's team of economists aims to understand Luxembourg's social and economic development in a comparative perspective and to contribute policy-relevant research to the national debate and the international scientific community. Research fields primarily include entrepreneurship, productivity, well-being.

More details on STATEC and STATEC Research are available here: https://statistiques.public.lu/en/statistique-publique/statec/red.html

The successful candidate will conduct empirical analysis and research on subjects of policy relevance in the area of entrepreneurship, and support the implementation of the Global Entrepreneurship Monitor (GEM) in Luxembourg. The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong interest in developing a research agenda on entrepreneurship, and be highly motivated to work in a policy-oriented research institution.

Main responsibilities:

  • Produce, manage and analyse data for the measurement of entrepreneurial activity in Luxembourg, including the GEM surveys;
  • Conduct quantitative analysis and prepare associated reports on topics related to entrepreneurship to provide policy-relevant evidence and insights for the Luxembourg economy as a whole;
  • Conduct research on the same topics to contribute to the international scientific community, e.g. through publications and presentations;
  • Contribute to the development of the research agenda of the organization;
  • Participate in a collaborative research environment, such as joint research projects, outreach activities, seminars, and grant proposals;
  • Establish cooperation and share knowledge with STATEC’s statistical production services; and
  • Disseminate research findings, methodological developments and analysis results to both scientific and wider audiences, including public officials, policy makers, statisticians.

Candidate's profile:

  • PhD in Economics or a closely related quantitative discipline;
  • Strong background in applied microeconomics and quantitative methods, with an interest in policy relevant research;
  • Proven experience working with individual-level datasets;
  • Previous publications, particularly in the area of entrepreneurship, are an asset;
  • Strong expertise in STATA;
  • Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills;
  • Ability to meet deadlines and work both as part of a team and independently; and
  • Strong written and oral communication skills in English - the working language of the department.

Desirable additional qualities include:

  • Previous research in small business economics and innovation economics;
  • Experience in survey design and survey implementation;
  • Knowledge of policy evaluation tools;
  • Machine learning techniques;
  • R and other programming languages; and
  • French/German/Luxembourgish.

How to apply

  • The closing date for applications is 31/12/2026. To apply, please provide a cover letter, full CV, name of two referees, and PhD transcript. Applications should clearly state the reference ASBL/2026-02. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview in late January or early February 2027.
  • We are also interviewing applicants at the following virtual event: 2026/27 European Job Market of Economists (EJME). In this context, interviews will be held virtually from December 14, 2026 to December 17, 2026, through recognized and easy-to-use video-conferencing platforms. If you wish to be interviewed online at this event, please make this clear in your application and apply here before Friday, November 27, 2026. Early applications are encouraged.
  • All candidates will be contacted with the outcome of their application. Unfortunately, we are unable to provide feedback to those applicants who are not shortlisted. We would like to thank all candidates for their application and interest.
  • Enquiries should be addressed to research.recruit`at’statec.etat.lu quoting the reference ASBL/2026-02.

Data protection:

Personal data will be processed exclusively for the purposes of the recruitment process in accordance with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
name: STATEC Research ASBL

adtitle: Faculty Positions in Economics, Indian Institute of Management Bangalore
adtext:
The Economics Area at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM Bangalore) invites applications for faculty positions at all levels from candidates with strong research credentials or potential. While we welcome exceptional candidates from all fields of economics, we are particularly interested in the following areas:

  • Macroeconomics and Monetary Economics (JEL: E)

Contact Information

For queries regarding faculty positions at IIM Bangalore, please contact: dean.faculty@iimb.ac.in

adtext:
The Department of Economics and Management at the University of Padua invites expressions of interest for a fixed-term postdoctoral position funded by the ERC Consolidator Grant RESTATE – REthinking the Welfare STATE under Political Constraints in a Changing World (Grant Agreement No. 101232064), led by Professor Alessia Russo. RESTATE studies the design and sustainability of the welfare state when political constraints limit government commitment and economies face demographic change. It combines dynamic theory, quantitative heterogeneous-agent models, and computational methods to study public debt, social insurance, intergenerational redistribution, and growth-enhancing policies.

The appointment is for up to four years. The preferred starting date is September 2027, with flexibility for an earlier or later start. The position is full-time and research-only, with no teaching obligations, and offers substantial research support, including funding for data acquisition or creation. The successful candidate will be encouraged to pursue their own research agenda and collaborate within the RESTATE network.

We seek candidates with strong research potential and interests aligned with RESTATE, particularly in macroeconomics, public finance, political economy, or related fields. Expertise in dynamic contracting, limited commitment, quantitative macroeconomics or computational methods is especially welcome.

Applicants must hold a PhD in Economics or a related field by the starting date. The contractual arrangement will depend on the candidate’s profile and eligibility under University of Padua regulations. The working language is English; knowledge of Italian is not required. We are committed to diversity and inclusion and strongly encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds. Compensation is competitive with that offered by comparable European research institutions. Researchers relocating to Italy may also qualify for favorable tax treatment under current Italian legislation.

The Department offers an active international research environment with regular seminars and workshops and a PhD programme in Economics and Management. It is located in Padua’s historic city center, in a lively university city with a large international community.

Applications should be submitted via EconJobMarket by November 30, 2026, and must include:

a. A cover letter;

b. A curriculum vitae;

c. A job market paper;

d. A research proposal;

e. Two letters of recommendation.

Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed virtually in December 2026 through the European Economic Association Job Market interview platform.

For further information, please contact Professor Alessia Russo at restateerc@gmail.com.
department: Department of Economics and Management "Marco Fanno"
